speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance; to help you, I need to ask a few questions. First, have these symptoms been present constantly, or do they come and go in spells?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) or Vestibular Neuritis. The description of a low-grade, constant spinning sensation since this morning, combined with nausea and relief from antihistamines, suggests a vestibular issue. The recent garlic intake is likely incidental but could indicate an upper respiratory infection triggering vestibular neuritis. To confirm the diagnosis, I need to know if your symptoms worsen significantly when you roll over in bed or tilt your head. REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike maneuver.
